published_results.claim: Restored chats no longer sit blank for about 0.7 s waiting on the file watcher, and they skip an extra ~300 ms skeleton ... file opens skip a Monaco wrapper that cost 50–65 ms each time
published_results.metric: UI latency removed (restored-chat blank time, skeleton time, per-file-open wrapper cost)
published_results.value: about 0.7 s + ~300 ms removed on chat restore; 50–65 ms removed per file open

published_results.claim: `bun run perf:render [--runs N] [--out file] [--cpu N] [--scenario a,b] [playwright args]` is an opt-in ... the runner reports medians and run-to-run spread
published_results.metric: Client render cost per scenario (React profiler commits/self ms, long tasks, rAF frame gaps p50/p95/max, CDP main-thread ms, heap delta) on replayed deterministic event streams
published_results.value: No results committed (default output goes to $TMPDIR/thinkrail-render-profile.json)

summary: ThinkRail publishes no benchmark or evaluation results: README and docs make no quantitative performance claims, and the only numbers are release-blog speed notes for 0.3.0 (about 0.7 s and ~300 ms removed from chat restore, 50–65 ms per file open) with no method or data. It does ship a well-specified opt-in Playwright render-profiling harness (bun run perf:render, e2e/perf/) that measures client rendering on replayed streams. The harness writes to a temp file, and no output is committed.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
